findings.description: UNCHANGED. ServiceInvalidatesTheEventConnectionInventoryScopedToThatConnection still constructs WebhookIntakeService directly and passes the ArrInventoryCacheProvider through the optional 'inventory' constructor argument, so it verifies the service logic but not that the production composition root injects the cache. No committed test resolves the hosted WebhookIntakeService from the service registrator and asserts its inventory dependency is present: RegistratorRegistersTheBoundedWebhookIntake only asserts the IHostedService descriptor, and the constructor dependency remains optional (ArrInventoryCacheProvider? inventory = null). A wiring regression would silently disable the shipped webhook invalidation without failing this test. Mitigations remain: ArrInventoryCacheProvider is registered at ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:80 and CreateLibraryReconciliationService uses GetRequiredService<ArrInventoryCacheProvider>() at line 246, so removing the registration fails ConfigurationReconciliationTriggerTests.RegistratorRegistersThePostSaveTriggerAsAHostedService. I independently confirmed the webhook invalidation test is behaviorally sensitive (throwaway mutation D: commenting out InvalidateInventory(webhookEvent, snapshot) failed the test at line 248) and scoped (radarr set invalidated, sonarr set retained).
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/WebhookBoundaryTests.cs:427-445 (descriptor-only registrator assertion; no inventory dependency assertion)
Throwaway mutation D: commented out InvalidateInventory(webhookEvent, snapshot) -> Failed 1 (line 248), confirming test sensitivity
findings.recommended_action: Optional: add a committed test that resolves the hosted WebhookIntakeService from the registrator and asserts its inventory dependency is present, or make the constructor dependency non-optional so a missing registration fails composition. Carried forward; no 11.3 acceptance criterion depends on it.

findings.description: UNCHANGED. The else branch in WebhookIntakeService.InvalidateInventory (bounded InvalidateAll when the event's connection cannot be resolved) still has no test. I independently confirmed the branch is unreachable with the current catalog shape: ArrConnectionCatalog.FromSnapshot always returns exactly the Sonarr and Radarr connections (ArrConnectionCatalog.cs returns a fixed two-element array), so ResolveConnection never returns null. The worker report records this as defensive and unreachable; the gap is documented, not hidden.
findings.recommended_action: None required while the catalog shape guarantees both connections; revisit if the catalog can omit a connection.

findings.description: UNCHANGED. InvalidationApiTakesOnlyTheNonSecretConnectionIdentifier is a structural reflection assertion (parameter type ArrConnectionId, bool/void return, exactly 4 declared methods), not behavioral. It supports the secret-free-surface claim but is brittle to any additional public Invalidate/InvalidateAll method and observes no behavior. Acceptable for an API-shape claim.

NEW. AllowedProviderEndpointPaths admits /api/v3/system/status, but that path is only used by RadarrClient/SonarrClient.ProbeAsync (private SystemStatusPath constant) and ProbeAsync has no caller anywhere in src; the reconciliation reads exercised by the test never issue it. The allowlist therefore widens the pin beyond the read set, so an injected request to /api/v3/system/status would not fail the negative test, and the test's XML doc calls the six paths 'the complete set of provider endpoints ArrTags is permitted to call for reconciliation reads', which is inaccurate for the probe-only path. This does not undermine the stated negative-dependency claim: ADR-018's research explicitly classifies /system/status as not a library revision token, and the query-key allowlist would still catch a revision/history query on any path. No false confidence for the 'no revision token / history/since / conditional request' acceptance criterion results.
evidence: grep: no .ProbeAsync( caller in src/ArrTags (excluding bin/obj); readers/factory never probe
docs/decisions.md:2310-2312 (ADR-018 research: /system/status is not a library revision token)
findings.recommended_action: Optional cleanup: drop '/api/v3/system/status' from AllowedProviderEndpointPaths so the pin is exactly the read/negotiation set the readers issue, or correct the XML doc to say the pin is the read set plus the probe path. No acceptance criterion depends on this.

summary: Attempt-2 correction round verified. TQ-11.3-1 is CLOSED: the negative-dependency test now pins the provider endpoint path allowlist and the query-key allowlist, and I independently reproduced sensitivity with two throwaway-copy mutations (unlisted /api/v3/history?page=1 fails at the path assertion; allowed path with an unlisted 'since' query key fails at the query-key assertion). TQ-11.3-2 is CLOSED: the per-source reconciliation test now observes the seeded set served before and no longer served after, and removing InvalidateInventory() fails it. TQ-11.3-3 remains open (LOW, unchanged): the webhook invalidation is still verified off the production composition root with an optional dependency, though the webhook test is behaviorally sensitive and scoped and the registration removal is caught by another test. TQ-11.3-4 and TQ-11.3-5 are unchanged informational notes. One new LOW (TQ-11.3-6, matching implementation-review 11.3-F6): the endpoint allowlist admits the probe-only /api/v3/system/status, which the reads never call, so the pin is slightly wider than the read set and the test's XML doc overstates it; this does not undermine the revision-token/history claim because ADR-018 classifies system/status as not a library revision token. Independently re-run: build 0 warnings/0 errors; focused classes 70 passed / 0 skipped / 70 total (twice); full default suite 1418 passed / 63 skipped / 1481 total. No 11.3 test is skipped, determinism is sound, and the tests exercise the real production types with only the network and the Jellyfin enumeration boundary doubled. No BLOCKER or HIGH remains; PASS_WITH_FINDINGS.
